title: A 20-Foot Wall of Water Races Up This River at 25 mph

scenes.text: A wall of water races up a river in China against the current.
It's the Qiantang River tidal bore, often called the biggest tidal bore on the planet.
The river narrows like a funnel, so the rising ocean tide gets squeezed into one huge wave.
It can stand around twenty feet tall and move faster than twenty-five miles an hour.
Thousands of people line the banks to watch it roar past every year.
A wave that runs backwards up a river.

description:
The Qiantang River tidal bore squeezes an ocean tide into a wall of water that races upstream at over 25 mph.
Waves can reach about 20 feet, and thousands watch it each year.
Would you stand on the bank?
first_comment: Would you watch it from the bank or surf it?
